bylaws.documentTitle: Dallas Chapter Bylaws (amended March 8, 2023; approved by the Area One Parliamentarian March 14, 2023)
bylaws.keeper: Parliamentarian (Lady Shirley Ison-Newsome), chair of the Bylaws Committee

sections.summary: Serve the community; sponsor Top Teens of America; promote meaningful living for senior citizens; improve the status of women; preserve the physical beauty of America; and collaborate with community, business, educational, and governmental partners.

Candidates subscribe to TLOD principles, bring a range of talents and skills, and are willing to serve. A college degree is not required. A convicted felon is not eligible. Applications go to the Membership Chair by the stated deadline.

Regular members meet all chapter obligations (finance, attendance, other requirements), pay chapter, Area, and National dues and assessments, and take part in programs. Life Members have 10+ years of membership, were continuously active the 5 years before applying, paid the one-time life fee, and pay annual chapter dues.

Two letters of recommendation; chapter vote by secret ballot; written notice of acceptance and fees; orientation at least 10 days before induction; two weeks to accept in writing. Fees are non-refundable and non-transferable. Induction is in the fall and/or spring using the National ritual, conducted by a National officer or Parliament-Top appointee. No pictures during the ceremony.
President, First Vice President, Second Vice President, Recording Secretary, Financial Secretary, Treasurer, Editor of the Crown, and Top Teen Advisor.
Parliamentarian, Historian, Sergeant-at-Arms, Chaplain, Corresponding Secretary, Assistant Recording Secretary, Assistant Corresponding Secretary, and Assistant Top Teen Advisor.
Active, financial members in good standing for at least one year who have attended meetings regularly.

Elected every two years by secret ballot at the May regular meeting of a Syn-Lod year; installed at the end of the June meeting. Two-year terms; no more than two consecutive terms in the same office. Highest vote count wins.

A two-thirds vote of the Executive Board may suspend an elected officer for neglect of duties or conduct unbecoming an officer. Resignations go to the Executive Board, then to the chapter for approval.

President presides and appoints committees (ex officio on all but Nominating). First VP assists the President and chairs the program thrusts. Second VP chairs Projects and coordinates public relations and awards. Recording Secretary keeps minutes, rosters, attendance. Financial Secretary collects dues and gives all money to the Treasurer. Treasurer deposits and pays signed orders. Top Teen Advisor supervises the Top Teens Program of Work. Editor of the Crown edits chapter news.
sections.note: 2025-2026 practice: the Second Vice President has led membership and intake; confirm assignments.

sections.summary: Every officer except the Treasurer delivers files, supplies, and materials to her successor within 30 days of the first meeting of the new year. The Treasurer turns in her report at the first meeting in September.
All elected and appointed officers plus the Past Presidents. It oversees all operations; its actions must be presented to the chapter for approval or ratification.

The Finance Committee (Treasurer as chair, Financial Secretary, First Vice President, and two appointees) develops the budget before November from the Program Committee's annual programs; the chapter votes in December.
sections.note: 2025-2026 practice: budget voted September 18, 2025; Finance chaired by Lady Tunia Hughes.

sections.summary: Five members elected from the floor by majority vote at the September meeting; they name their chair. The slate is presented at the April meeting.

sections.summary: Standing: Executive Board, Bylaws, Finance, Service to Youth, Projects, Scholarship, Public Relations, Nominating, Membership, Courtesy, Devotion, Senior Citizens, Status of Women, Community Beautification, Community Partnership, Founders Day, Archives, Awards, Social. Special: Protocol, Blue and Silver Ball, Conference, President's Council, Election, Juanita M. Johns Luncheon, Lords, Social Media, Technology.

The chapter year opens the first Wednesday in September and closes the first Wednesday in June. Meetings are the first Wednesday of each month at 6:00 PM unless changed by majority vote. The President may call additional meetings. Virtual meetings are allowed at the Executive Board's discretion.
